summary: Independent verification of the 'blocked date still bookable by patient' bug. Confirmed the REAL, still-open server-side gap that E1 missed. Public GETs (blocked-dates, booked-slots) correctly reflect the block (so the calendar UI does grey out the date — that's why E1's manual UI test appeared to work), BUT the actual booking-CREATION and RESCHEDULE endpoints have NO validation against doctor_schedules.blocked_dates / blocked_sessions. A determined patient (or any patient with a stale/cached page, back-button, race condition, or API replay) can POST /api/appointments (or /appointments/{id}/reschedule) directly with the blocked date and it is accepted with 200 OK. This perfectly matches the user's repeated 'slots are still seen / still bookable' complaint. Ran 9 pytest tests: 5 passed (GETs work), 4 failed (POST-create Vikas, POST-create Neha, POST-create online mode, POST-reschedule — all wrongly accepted).

critical.issue: Does NOT validate against doctor_schedules.blocked_dates. Booking on a blocked date returns 200 and inserts the appointment. Reproduces for Pushpa Clinic AND for 'online' clinic value. This is the true root cause of the user's repeated complaint.

Same gap as /api/appointments — no blocked_dates / blocked_sessions check before insert. (Not exercised end-to-end here because it requires an OTP, but code review of lines 717-816 confirms no such check exists.)
Does NOT validate against blocked_dates / blocked_sessions. Successfully rescheduled an appointment onto Dr. Vikas Jha's blocked-leave date (200 OK, booking_id DGO-...). Ref lines 1624-1698.

minor.issue: Also does not check blocked_sessions (partial-day session blocks). If a doctor blocks only 11:00-14:00, a POST with a time inside that window still succeeds. Same code path as the blocked_dates gap above.

ui_bugs.issue: Confirmed known cosmetic gap: date-scroller only excludes Sundays, NOT blocked_dates. Patient can visually select a blocked date; underlying slot list correctly shows no available times, but combined with the backend reschedule gap above this becomes exploitable — a determined patient can click a greyed-time-slot pattern or hit the API directly and the reschedule will succeed.

blockedDates state is fetched via useEffect only on [doctor] change (line ~102-119) — it does NOT refresh while the modal stays open. A patient who has the /diagyn page open BEFORE the doctor blocks a date will keep seeing the old un-greyed calendar until they refresh. This is a stale-state race window that, combined with the backend gap, exactly matches 'slots are still seen'.

integration_issues.flow: Public booking (any doctor, any clinic incl. 'online') on a blocked date
integration_issues.issue: Frontend calendar correctly hides/greys the date (verified via GET /api/doctors/blocked-dates and GET /api/appointments/booked-slots which both return the block). BUT backend accepts the booking if bypassed — so any stale page, back-button, direct API call, or race condition slips through.

action_items: PRIMARY FIX: In POST /api/appointments (appointment_routes.py line 137-246), after normalize_date_format but before the insert, look up db.doctor_schedules for the doctor and reject with HTTPException 400 if input.date is in blocked_dates, or if (input.date, input.time) falls within any blocked_sessions window. Reuse the exact lookup logic from get_doctor_schedule_by_name() / the get_slots endpoint (lines 630-680) — the same is_slot_blocked_by_session helper already exists at line 647 and can be extracted into a shared helper.
Apply the SAME check to POST /api/appointments/guest (line 717-816) — insert after the existing slot-conflict check on line 757-763.
Apply the SAME check to POST /api/appointments/{id}/reschedule (line 1624-1698) — insert after the 'existing slot' check on line 1666-1675.
Recommend factoring out the check into a helper e.g. `async def _assert_slot_not_blocked(db, doctor_name, date, time)` and calling it from all three endpoints.

OPTIONAL UI polish (not the root cause but improves UX): (a) refetch blockedDates in DoctorDetailModal on modal-open AND on a short interval / websocket / socket signal so a stale page updates; (b) MyAppointmentsPage.jsx reschedule date-scroller should also skip dates present in blocked_dates, not just Sundays.
critical_code_review_comments: appointment_routes.py already has all the plumbing (get_doctor_schedule_by_name at line 534, blocked_dates + blocked_sessions handled inside GET /booked-slots at line 578-608 and GET /doctors/schedule-slots at line 632-683). The AUTHORING pattern is clearly there — it just was not applied to the create/reschedule paths. Very likely an oversight during the earlier fix session which only touched staff booking + GET endpoints.

Recommend a single shared helper `is_slot_blocked(doctor_name, date, time) -> tuple[bool, str]` used by GET (to hide) AND POST (to reject). Currently the logic is duplicated inline in GET, which is why the create path was missed.

Note: E1's manual UI test 'appeared to work' because the calendar correctly greys the date on a fresh page load — but that only tests the GET/UI layer, not the actual server-side booking authorization. Any determined user, cached page, or race condition bypasses this.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: appointment_routes.py has three appointment-writing endpoints (POST /appointments line 137, POST /appointments/guest line 717, POST /appointments/{id}/reschedule line 1624). All three query db.appointments for existing bookings on the same slot, but NONE of them query db.doctor_schedules for blocked_dates / blocked_sessions. The doctor's leave is stored in db.doctor_schedules by /doctor-schedule/block-date (writes to blocked_dates array). GET /appointments/booked-slots correctly consults this collection and returns date_blocked=True, which is why the calendar UI works. But because the CREATE side does not, any bypass of the UI (stale cached page, back-button, direct API call, mobile-app race, or simply refreshing after a doctor blocks a date while the patient already has the booking form filled) will successfully write an appointment onto a leave day. REPRODUCTION: 1) Login as dr_vikas, POST /api/doctor-schedule/block-date with a future date. 2) Verify GET /api/doctors/blocked-dates lists it (it does). 3) POST /api/appointments with that date+any valid clinic-hour time → returns 200 Booked. Same for /appointments/guest (with OTP) and /appointments/{id}/reschedule. MITIGATION: Add a `_assert_slot_not_blocked` helper (see action_items) and call it from all three write endpoints immediately before insert/update.
